# Limitations

The primary sparse-relay claim is scoped to Gemma 3 270M, one dictionary and
task, and lexical rather than semantic outcomes. Gemma 3 1B supplies an
exploratory sparse steerability audit and a matched natural-residual
replication; it does not supply an identified sparse transmission phenotype.
Greedy results are supplemented by exact
two-article stochastic mixtures, not unrestricted vocabulary sampling. S1 was
attribution-selected and amplified by up to \(5\times\), so we decompose
this handle rather than a unique ontology; large gain may be off-manifold.
S2 often derails; the L5/F383 localization is exploratory and post-selection
on the evaluation prompts, may encode a vowel class, and has only four
matched controls (\(p=0.20\)). S1's leftover overlaps its random control;
the switched subset is descriptive; the twin estimate is small-\(N\); and
TV is nonadditive.

The synthetic pair validates estimand polarity, not transformer behavior.
The pre-article patch establishes sensitivity on 12 held-out pairs but is
target-constructed, vocabulary-cued, a full residual transplant, and
subthreshold: private-route capacity, not a sparse plan. All 12 pairs are
consonant-native, so inserted `an` is mismatched for both alternatives.
Layer selection uses four development pairs. The interaction shows
article-prefix compatibility, not a meaningful allocation trade-off.
Model-family, task, sampling, and prompt-controlled route allocation remain
open. The effect-matched 1B coalition uses 24 features at \(20\times\), often
pushes `a/an` below other tokens, and is therefore off-manifold or
mediator-invalid for the intended channel comparison. All 1B selection graphs
hit the 1,200-node cap (mean selected/active ratio 0.608), so unequal graph
coverage remains a plausible contributor to sparse-selection failure.

The float32 audit casts only the final normalization and unembedding; it
does not rerun the transformer or CLT in float32. Natural residual patches
are full-state transplants selected at one pooled development layer. They
show private target influence but no article change, so they do not
establish causal allocation or a public/private regime switch. The
32-feature attribution calibration has adequate resolution for moderate
monotone effects, not proof of zero association; its bootstrap intervals are
wide for downstream outcomes, and its intervention gain remains \(5\times\).

**Ethics.** This public-model study uses synthetic prompts and no human or
personal data. We mitigate overclaiming through scoped conclusions and
released code/results. AI-agent assistance is declared in the NeurIPS
checklist.
